@client_factory.event(PairStatusEv)
async def PairStatusMessage(_: NewAClient, message: PairStatusEv):
    log.info(f"logged as {message.ID.User}")


async def run_factory():
    await client_factory.run()
    # Do something else
    await client_factory.idle_all()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # all created clients will be automatically logged in and receive all
    # events
    asyncio.run(run_factory())

items.title: Resume or create
items.text:
factory = ClientFactory("db.sqlite3")

for device in factory.get_all_devices():   # stored sessions
    factory.new_client(device.JID)

factory.new_client(uuid="extra-bot")       # fresh pairing slot

items.title: One handler set for all clients
items.text: @factory.event(...) receives events from every managed client; the first handler argument identifies which client fired it.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
await factory.idle_all() connects everything and parks; SIGINT schedules await factory.stop() for a clean shutdown.

The sync variant is available in examples/multisession.py.

items.title: Pairing by Phone Number
items.text:
Pair a device without scanning a QR code. PairPhone returns an 8-character code that you type into the linked-device dialog on the phone.

from neonize.client import NewClient
from neonize.events import ConnectedEv, MessageEv
from neonize.proto.waCommon_pb2 import ClientName

client = NewClient("session.db")

@client.event(ConnectedEv)
def on_connected(client: NewClient, _: ConnectedEv) -> None:
    print("Connected")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    code = client.PairPhone(
        "628123456789",                  # international format, digits only
        show_push_notification=True,
        client_name=ClientName.LINUX,
    )
    print(f"Enter this code in WhatsApp: {code}")
    client.connect()                     # completes pairing with the code

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Run the script.
  2. On the phone open Settings > Linked Devices > Link a Device.
  3. Choose Link with phone number instead.
  4. Type the printed code.

The session is stored like any QR pairing; subsequent runs connect without prompting.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• show_push_notification=True raises a notification on the target phone.
  • The code expires after a short window; rerun to get a fresh one.
  • The same flow exists on the async client: await client.PairPhone(...).

items.title: Authentication
items.text: WhatsApp multidevice supports two linking methods. Both produce the same result: a persistent session stored in your SQLite database.

items.title: Method 1: QR Code (default)
items.text:
Calling client.connect() with an empty session store prints a QR code to the terminal. Scan it from the phone:

from neonize.client import NewClient

client = NewClient("session.db")
client.connect()

items.title: Custom QR handling
items.text:
Pass qrCallback to render the QR yourself — for example in a web UI. The callback receives the client and the raw PNG bytes of the QR image.

from neonize.client import NewClient

def on_qr(client: NewClient, qr_png: bytes) -> None:
    # qr_png is a PNG-encoded QR image; serve it, save it, or print it.
    with open("qr.png", "wb") as f:
        f.write(qr_png)

client = NewClient("session.db")
client.connect()

QR rotation

WhatsApp rotates QR codes periodically while pairing is pending. The callback fires again for each refresh until the code is scanned or it times out.

items.title: Method 2: Phone-Number Link Code
items.text:
PairPhone returns an 8-character code that you enter on the phone instead of scanning anything. Useful for headless servers where showing a QR is inconvenient.

from neonize.client import NewClient
from neonize.utils.enum import ClientType
from neonize.proto.waCommon_pb2 import ClientName

client = NewClient("session.db")

code: str = client.PairPhone(
    "628123456789",          # phone number in international format, no + or spaces
    show_push_notification=True,
    client_name=ClientName.LINUX,
)
print(f"Enter this code on your phone: {code}")

Then on the phone: Settings > Linked Devices > Link a Device > Link with phone number instead, and type the code.

items.title: Reconnecting
items.text:
Nothing special is required — construct the client with the same database file and connect:

client = NewClient("session.db")   # loads the stored session
client.connect()                   # no QR, straight to ConnectedEv

To resume a specific session when the database holds several, pass its JID:

from neonize.utils import build_jid

client = NewClient("session.db", jid=build_jid("628123456789"))

items.title: Multi-Device Sessions
items.text:
One SQLite file can hold multiple linked devices, each identified by a UUID.

work = NewClient("session.db", uuid="work-bot")
home = NewClient("session.db", uuid="home-bot")

See Sessions and Storage and the multi-session example.

items.title: Logging Out
items.text:
logout() unlinks the device and clears the stored session. The next connect will require pairing again.

client.logout()

Irreversible

After logout the session cannot be recovered — pair again via QR or link code.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer
  • FFmpeg (required for media conversion: stickers, audio, video, thumbnails)

items.title: Install from PyPI
items.text:
pipuv 
pip install neonize

uv add neonize

The PyPI wheel ships the compiled Go core (.so / .dll / .dylib) inside the package. There is nothing else to download at runtime — the native library is loaded directly from the wheel on import.

Platform detection

Neonize selects the correct binary for your platform at import time via neonize.utils.platform. If no matching binary exists, an UnsupportedPlatform error is raised with the exact filename it looked for.

items.title: Install FFmpeg
items.text:
Sticker and audio/video handling shell out to FFmpeg for transcoding.

Debian / UbuntuFedoramacOS (Homebrew)Windows (winget) 
sudo apt install ffmpeg

sudo dnf install ffmpeg

brew install ffmpeg

winget install Gyan.FFmpeg

Text-only bots that never send or convert media work without FFmpeg.

items.title: Verify the Installation
items.text:
import neonize

print(neonize.__version__)
from neonize.client import NewClient  # noqa: E402  (loads the native core)

If this prints a version and imports cleanly, both the Python layer and the Go core are functional.

items.title: Installing from Source
items.text: Building from source requires Go 1.25+, protoc, and a C compiler. See Building from Source for the full toolchain.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: This page builds a working echo bot in under five minutes.

items.title: 1. Create the Client
items.text:
from neonize.client import NewClient

client = NewClient("session.db")

The name argument is the path of the SQLite file where the session is persisted. On the first run it is created empty; on every later run the stored session is reused and no re-pairing is needed.

items.title: 2. Register Event Handlers
items.text:
Handlers are plain functions decorated with @client.event(EventType). Each handler receives the client instance and the typed event object.

from neonize.client import NewClient
from neonize.events import ConnectedEv, MessageEv, PairStatusEv

@client.event(PairStatusEv)
def on_paired(client: NewClient, event: PairStatusEv) -> None:
    print(f"Paired as {event.ID.User}")

@client.event(ConnectedEv)
def on_connected(client: NewClient, event: ConnectedEv) -> None:
    print("Connected to WhatsApp")

@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, message: MessageEv) -> None:
    ...

items.title: 3. Handle Incoming Messages
items.text:
MessageEv carries two important members:

Member Description message.Message The protobuf Message payload (conversation text, image, document, ...) message.Info.MessageSource.Chat The JID of the chat the message belongs to 
@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, message: MessageEv) -> None:
    from neonize import extract_text

    text = extract_text(message.Message)
    chat = message.Info.MessageSource.Chat

    if text == "ping":
        client.reply_message("pong", message)

extract_text() handles plain text, extended text (with mentions/links), and the caption fields of image, video and document messages in one call.

items.title: 4. Connect
items.text:
client.connect()

On the first run a QR code is printed to the terminal — scan it with WhatsApp (Settings > Linked Devices > Link a Device). The session is then stored and every future connect() reuses it silently.

items.title: Complete Example
items.text:
from neonize.client import NewClient
from neonize.events import ConnectedEv, MessageEv

client = NewClient("session.db")

@client.event(ConnectedEv)
def on_connected(client: NewClient, _: ConnectedEv) -> None:
    print("Connected")

@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, message: MessageEv) -> None:
    from neonize import extract_text

    text = extract_text(message.Message)
    chat = message.Info.MessageSource.Chat

    if text == "ping":
        client.reply_message("pong", message)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    client.connect()

Run it:

python bot.py

items.title: Next Steps
items.text:
• Pair without scanning a QR code: Authentication
  • Send images, videos, documents and stickers: Sending Messages
  • Understand the event system in depth: Event Model
  • Use asyncio instead of threads: Async Client

Phone number strings

You can pass a phone number string directly to send_message() without building a JID first:

client.send_message("6281234567890", "Hello!")

items.title: Constructor Options
items.text:
from neonize.client import NewClient

client = NewClient(
    "session.db",          # SQLite session path
    jid=None,              # resume a specific stored session
    props=None,            # DeviceProps protobuf (device branding)
    uuid=None,             # session key when several share one database
    new_device=False,      # force pairing a fresh device for this uuid
)

items.title: Connecting Through a Proxy
items.text:
Route the WhatsApp WebSocket through an HTTP/SOCKS proxy:

from neonize.utils import ProxySettings   # configure per your deployment

client.connect_with_proxy(proxy_settings)

A proxy can also be changed at runtime with set_proxy_address, and the current address read back:

client.set_proxy_address("socks5://127.0.0.1:1080")

items.title: Disappearing Messages
items.text:
Set the default timer applied to new chats, or per chat:

from datetime import timedelta

client.set_default_disappearing_timer(timedelta(days=7))  # account default
client.set_disappearing_timer(chat_jid, timedelta(hours=24))  # one chat

timedelta(0) disables the timer. Raises SetDisappearingTimerError / SetDefaultDisappearingTimerError.

items.title: Delivery Receipts
items.text:
Force delivery receipts even while offline syncing:

client.set_force_activate_delivery_receipts(True)

Useful for bots that must not miss message acknowledgement windows.

items.title: Passive Mode
items.text:
Suppress outgoing presence and receipt traffic (useful for archive-only listeners):

client.set_passive(True)

items.title: Stopping
items.text:
Method Behavior disconnect() Drop the connection; session stays valid stop() Disconnect and stop background workers logout() Unlink the device and clear the session

For the async client, prefer await client.stop() or the shared ClientFactory.stop() — see Async Best Practices.

items.title: Message Retry Control
items.text:
When a message cannot be decrypted, Neonize participates in WhatsApp's retry protocol. Override the handler to customize behavior:

custom = client.get_message_for_retry(msg_bytes, source)   # inspect/replace payload

items.title: Runtime Introspection
items.text:
me = client.get_me()               # own JID and profile info
version = client.generate_message_id()  # helper for custom flows

items.title: Checking Registration
items.text:
Before messaging a number, verify it is on WhatsApp:

from neonize.utils import build_jid

results = client.is_on_whatsapp([build_jid("628123456789")])
if results[0].IsIn:
    ...

Raises IsOnWhatsAppError when the check fails at protocol level.

items.title: User Info
items.text:
info = client.get_user_info(user_jid)   # business profile, status, picture metadata

Raises GetUserInfoError on failure.

items.title: Profile Pictures
items.text:
pic = client.get_profile_picture(chat)          # URL of the current picture

Picture changes arrive as PictureEv.

items.title: Local Contact Store
items.text:
The ContactStore persists contacts in SQLite:

all_contacts = client.contact.get_all_contacts()

items.title: Your presence
items.text:
from neonize.utils.enum import Presence

client.send_presence(Presence.AVAILABLE)    # online
client.send_presence(Presence.UNAVAILABLE)  # offline

items.title: Per-chat typing indicators
items.text:
from neonize.utils.enum import ChatPresence, ChatPresenceMedia

client.send_chat_presence(chat, ChatPresence.COMPOSING, ChatPresenceMedia.TEXT)
# ... preparing reply ...
client.send_chat_presence(chat, ChatPresence.PAUSED, ChatPresenceMedia.TEXT)

Raises SendPresenceError if the server rejects the update. Incoming indicators from other users arrive as ChatPresenceEv.

items.title: Subscribing to a contact's presence
items.text:
client.subscribe_presence(user_jid)

After subscribing, presence updates for that user arrive as PresenceEv.

items.title: Privacy Settings
items.text:
settings = client.get_privacy_settings()     # current values

Change one value:

from neonize.proto.waAdv.WAAdv_pb2 import PrivacySettingType
from neonize.utils.enum import ...           # value enums per setting

client.set_privacy_setting(PrivacySettingType.LAST_SEEN, value)

Changes (including ones made from the phone) arrive as PrivacySettingsEv.

Status-privacy readers:

for entry in client.get_status_privacy():
    print(entry)

items.title: Blocking
items.text:
blocklist = client.get_blocklist()

from neonize.proto.waE2E.WAWebProtobufsE2E_pb2 import BlocklistAction

client.update_blocklist(user_jid, BlocklistAction.BLOCK)
client.update_blocklist(user_jid, BlocklistAction.UNBLOCK)

Blocklist changes arrive as BlocklistEv / BlocklistChangeEv.

items.title: Own Profile
items.text:
me = client.get_me()
client.set_profile_name("My Bot")
client.set_profile_photo("avatar.png")
client.set_status_message("Building with Neonize")

items.title: Business Links
items.text:
target = client.resolve_business_message_link("https://wa.me/c/...")
qr_target = client.resolve_contact_qr_link("ABCD-1234")
link = client.get_contact_qr_link()      # generate your own QR link

items.title: Calls
items.text:
Reject an incoming call so it rings neither side:

from neonize.events import CallOfferEv
from neonize.exc import RejectCallError

@client.event(CallOfferEv)
def on_call(client: NewClient, ev: CallOfferEv) -> None:
    try:
        client.reject_call(ev.Call.From, ev.Info.ID)
    except RejectCallError as exc:
        log.warning("Failed to reject call: %s", exc)

items.title: Group Management
items.text: Group JIDs use the g.us server. Every method below takes or returns JID objects — see JID and Addressing.

items.title: Creating a Group
items.text:
from neonize.utils import build_jid

group = client.create_group(
    "Project Team",
    [build_jid("628123456789"), build_jid("628987654321")],
)
info: GroupInfo = client.get_group_info(group.JID)

items.title: Discovering Groups
items.text:
groups = client.get_joined_groups()        # list of linked-group metadata
for g in groups:
    print(g.GroupName, g.JID)

Community sub-groups are reachable through get_sub_groups(parent_jid) and get_linked_group_participants(group_jid).

items.title: Metadata and Invite Links
items.text:
info = client.get_group_info(group_jid)          # name, topic, participants, settings
info2 = client.get_group_info_from_link("https://chat.whatsapp.com/AbCdEf")
invite = client.get_group_invite_link(group_jid) # generate a shareable link

items.title: Joining
items.text:
client.join_group_with_link("https://chat.whatsapp.com/AbCdEf")
# or resolve first:
meta = client.get_group_info_from_invite("AbCdEf")
client.join_group_with_invite(meta)

items.title: Participants
items.text:
All operations take a list of JIDs plus an action:

from neonize.proto.waE2E.WAWebProtobufsE2E_pb2 import (
    ParticipantChangeType,   # ADD | REMOVE | PROMOTE | DEMOTE
)

client.update_group_participants(
    group_jid, [build_jid("628123456789")], ParticipantChangeType.ADD
)

Pending join requests can be inspected with get_group_request_participants.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Method Purpose Raises set_group_name(jid, name) Rename the group SetGroupNameError set_group_topic(jid, topic) Set description/topic SetGroupTopicError set_group_photo(jid, path_or_bytes) Change the picture SetGroupPhotoError set_group_announce(jid, locked) Only admins may send messages SetGroupAnnounceError set_group_locked(jid, locked) Only admins may edit group info SetGroupLockedError 
client.set_group_name(group_jid, "New Name")
client.set_group_announce(group_jid, True)      # admin-only chat

items.title: Leaving and Linking
items.text:
client.leave_group(group_jid)          # raises LeaveGroupError on failure

Communities (linked groups) connect child groups to a parent:

client.link_group(child_jid, parent_jid)
client.unlink_group(child_jid, parent_jid)

create_group also accepts linked_parent= / group_parent= to create directly inside a community.

items.title: JoinedGroup Event
items.text:
When the bot is added to a group you receive JoinedGroupEv, which since v0.4.3 carries who performed the add:

from neonize.events import JoinedGroupEv

@client.event(JoinedGroupEv)
def on_joined(client: NewClient, ev: JoinedGroupEv) -> None:
    if ev.Sender is not None:
        print(f"Added by {ev.Sender.User}")
    client.send_message(ev.JID, "Thanks for adding me! Type /help.")

Ongoing changes to groups you are in arrive as GroupInfoEv.

items.title: Creating a poll
items.text:
from neonize.utils.enum import VoteType

msg = client.build_poll_vote_creation(
    "Lunch?",                     # poll question
    ["Pizza", "Burger", "Sushi"], # options (2-12)
    VoteType.SINGLE,              # or VoteType.MULTIPLE
)
client.send_message(chat, msg)

Raises BuildPollVoteCreationError for invalid configurations.

items.title: Voting in a poll
items.text:
# Given a received poll message:
vote = client.build_poll_vote(poll_message_info, ["Pizza"])
client.send_message(chat, vote)

build_poll_vote encrypts the selection with the poll's message secret.

items.title: Reading incoming votes
items.text:
Poll votes arrive as MessageEv with a pollVoteMessage payload; decrypt the selected options with:

selected = client.decrypt_poll_vote(original_poll_msg, vote_msg)

items.title: Reactions
items.text:
reaction = client.build_reaction(chat, sender_jid, message_id, reaction="👍")
client.send_message(chat, reaction)

items.title: Interactive Buttons
items.text: The neonize.ext.interactive_message module provides typed builders that produce CustomInteractiveMessage payloads accepted by send_interactive_message.

items.title: Quick replies and URL buttons
items.text:
from neonize.ext.interactive_message import (
    ButtonMessage,
    ReplyButton,
    UrlButton,
)

message = ButtonMessage(
    title="Daily Report",
    body="Choose an action",
    footer="Neonize bot",
    buttons=[
        ReplyButton(display_text="Send report"),
        UrlButton(display_text="Dashboard", url="https://example.com"),
    ],
)
client.send_interactive_message(chat, message)

Available button types: ReplyButton, UrlButton, CallButton, CopyButton, LocationButton, AddressButton, ReminderButton, CancelReminderButton.

items.title: List selection
items.text:
from neonize.ext.interactive_message import (
    ButtonMessage, Row, Section, SelectionButton,
)

message = ButtonMessage(
    title="Settings",
    body="Pick an option",
    buttons=[
        SelectionButton(
            title="Options",
            sections=[
                Section(
                    title="General",
                    rows=[
                        Row(title="Language", description="Change language"),
                        Row(title="Theme", description="Light or dark"),
                    ],
                )
            ],
        )
    ],
)
client.send_interactive_message(chat, message)

items.title: Carousel
items.text: CarouselMessage lays out cards with images — see the module reference via API Utilities or the source at neonize/ext/interactive_message/.

items.title: Raw Protocol Access
items.text:
For flows the builders do not cover yet, compose the protobuf directly and send it as a plain message:

from neonize.proto.waE2E.WAWebProtobufsE2E_pb2 import (
    FutureProofMessage, InteractiveMessage, Message, MessageContextInfo,
)

payload = Message(
    viewOnceMessage=FutureProofMessage(
        message=Message(
            interactiveMessage=InteractiveMessage(
                body=InteractiveMessage.Body(text="Body"),
                footer=InteractiveMessage.Footer(text="Footer"),
                nativeFlowMessage=InteractiveMessage.NativeFlowMessage(
                    buttons=[
                        InteractiveMessage.NativeFlowMessage.NativeFlowButton(
                            name="quick_reply",
                            buttonParamsJSON='{"display_text":"Tap","id":"1"}',
                        )
                    ]
                ),
            )
        )
    )
)
client.send_message(chat, payload)

Fragility

Raw interactive payloads depend on undocumented WhatsApp internals. Prefer the ext builders; fall back to raw protobuf only when needed.

items.title: Sources Accepted
items.text:
Media methods accept three input kinds interchangeably:

Source Example Local path "/tmp/photo.jpg" Raw bytes open("photo.jpg", "rb").read() URL "https://example.com/photo.jpg" 
client.send_image(chat, "https://download.samplelib.com/png/sample-boat-400x300.png")

items.title: Sending Media
items.text:
# Image with caption, as a reply, marked view-once
client.send_image(chat, "photo.jpg", caption="Sunset", quoted=ev.Message, viewonce=True)

# Video with caption and GIF-style looping playback
client.send_video(chat, "clip.mp4", caption="Loop", gifplayback=True)

# Voice note (push-to-talk) vs music audio
client.send_audio(chat, "voice.ogg", ptt=True)
client.send_audio(chat, "song.mp3")

# Document with explicit filename shown to the recipient
client.send_document(chat, "report.pdf", filename="Q3-report.pdf", caption="Report")

items.title: Stickers
items.text:
send_sticker converts any image or short video into a WhatsApp sticker. FFmpeg is required for the conversion.

client.send_sticker(chat, "meme.png")
client.send_sticker(chat, "meme.png", name="Bot", packname="MyPack")  # with EXIF metadata

For multiple stickers at once:

files = ["1.png", "2.png", "3.webp"]
for msg in client.build_stickerpack_message(files, packname="Pack", publisher="Me"):
    client.send_message(chat, msg)

The pack builder chunks automatically (WhatsApp limits packs to 60 stickers, each under 1 MB).

items.title: Albums
items.text: responses = client.send_album(chat, ["a.jpg", "b.jpg"], caption="Gallery")

items.title: Uploading Without Sending
items.text:
To upload media once and reference it yourself:

from neonize.utils.enum import MediaType

resp = client.upload(png_bytes, MediaType.Photo)
print(resp.URL)   # hosted URL; resp.DirectPath, .MediaKey, ...

items.title: Downloading Incoming Media
items.text:
@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, ev: MessageEv) -> None:
    payload = ev.Message
    if payload.imageMessage:
        data = client.download_any(payload)             # bytes
        client.download_any(payload, f"img/{ev.Info.ID}.jpg")  # or save

items.title: Building Message Payloads Manually
items.text:
Every send method has a build_*_message counterpart returning a protobuf Message you can pass to send_message — useful for combining media with interactive elements:

msg = client.build_image_message("photo.jpg", caption="Built manually")
client.send_message(chat, msg)

Available builders: build_image_message, build_video_message, build_audio_message, build_document_message, build_sticker_message, build_stickerpack_message, build_album_content.

items.title: FFmpeg Notes
items.text:
• Required for sticker conversion and audio transcoding.
  • Thumbnails for videos/documents are extracted via neonize.utils.ffmpeg.
  • If FFmpeg is missing, conversion methods raise FFProbeError / ConvertStickerError; plain text sends are unaffected.

Size limits

WhatsApp rejects media above roughly 16 MB for images/audio and 100 MB for video/documents. Oversized uploads raise UploadError.

items.title: Newsletters and Channels
items.text: Channels (newsletters) are one-to-many broadcasts. Their JIDs use the newsletter server.

items.title: Creating a Channel
items.text:
meta = client.create_newsletter(
    "My Channel",
    "Daily updates about automation",
    "cover.png",          # local path, bytes or URL
)
print(meta.ID)            # newsletter JID for later use

Raises CreateNewsletterError on failure.

items.title: Resolving Channels
items.text:
from neonize.proto.Neonize_pb2 import NewsletterJID

# From an invite link (https://whatsapp.com/channel/<id>):
meta = client.get_newsletter_info_with_invite("https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va...")

# From a known JID:
meta = client.get_newsletter_info(newsletter_jid)

print(meta.ThreadMeta.MessageCount)   # message volume

Both raise GetNewsletterInfoError / GetNewsletterInfoWithInviteError respectively when the channel cannot be resolved.

items.title: Following and Unfollowing
items.text:
client.follow_newsletter(meta.ID)
client.unfollow_newsletter(meta.ID)

Membership changes also arrive as NewsletterJoinEv / NewsletterLeaveEv.

items.title: Reading Messages
items.text:
from neonize.types import MessageServerID

messages = client.get_newsletter_messages(meta.ID, 10, MessageServerID(0))
for m in messages:
    print(m.Key.ID)

MessageServerID(0) means "from the beginning"; otherwise pass the server ID of the oldest message you already have. Metadata updates arrive as NewsLetterMessageMetaEv.

items.title: Reacting
items.text:
Channel reactions are keyed by server ID, not message ID:

client.newsletter_send_reaction(meta.ID, MessageServerID(12345), "👍", "")

An empty reaction string removes it.

items.title: Muting and Live Updates
items.text:
client.newsletter_toggle_mute(meta.ID, True)     # mute

# Subscribe to live message updates for this channel:
resp = client.newsletter_subscribe_live_updates(meta.ID)

New channel messages then arrive through the normal event stream.

Marking messages as viewed (affects read stats on other clients):

client.newsletter_mark_viewed(meta.ID, [MessageServerID(12345)])

items.title: Uploading to a Channel
items.text:
resp = client.upload_newsletter(media_bytes, MediaType.Photo, newsletter_jid)

One-way traffic

Channels do not support replies from followers. Bots interact by following, reading, reacting and mirroring content — not by sending chat messages into them.

items.title: The MessageEv Event
items.text:
Everything arrives through MessageEv. The two members you need most:

from neonize.client import NewClient
from neonize.events import MessageEv

@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, ev: MessageEv) -> None:
    text = ev.Message.conversation or ev.Message.extendedTextMessage.text
    chat = ev.Info.MessageSource.Chat
    sender = ev.Info.MessageSource.Sender
Member Description ev.Message Protobuf Message — inspect fields to learn the content type ev.Info.ID Message ID; keep it for replies, reactions, mark-read, pinning ev.Info.MessageSource.Chat Destination JID (user, group or channel) ev.Info.MessageSource.Sender Actual sender JID (differs from Chat in groups) ev.Info.Timestamp Unix timestamp

items.title: Detecting Content Types
items.text:
The protobuf payload has one populated field per type:

m = ev.Message

if m.conversation:
    ...  # plain text
elif m.imageMessage:
    ...  # image — caption in .caption, media key for download
elif m.videoMessage:
    ...
elif m.audioMessage:
    ...  # ptt=True means voice note
elif m.documentMessage:
    ...  # filename in .fileName
elif m.extendedTextMessage:
    ...  # reply, link preview, or mention text
elif m.reactionMessage:
    ...

Text shortcut

Use extract_text() to get the text from any message type in one call:

from neonize import extract_text

text = extract_text(ev.Message)   # conversation, extendedText, caption, or ""

This covers plain text, extended text (mentions / links), and the caption fields of image, video and document messages.

items.title: Downloading Media
items.text:
download_any extracts the payload from any message and either returns the bytes or writes them to a path:

data: bytes = client.download_any(ev.Message)

client.download_any(ev.Message, "downloads/photo.jpg")   # saved to disk

Works with images, videos, audio, documents and stickers. See Media Handling.

items.title: Ignoring Your Own Messages and Status
items.text:
Filter early to keep handlers clean:

@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, ev: MessageEv) -> None:
    if ev.Info.MessageSource.Chat.Server == "broadcast":
        return                      # status updates
    if ev.Info.MessageSource.Sender == client.me.JID:
        return                      # own outgoing echo
    ...

items.title: Marking Messages as Read
items.text:
from neonize.utils.enum import ReceiptType

client.mark_read(
    ev.Info.ID,
    chat=ev.Info.MessageSource.Chat,
    sender=ev.Info.MessageSource.Sender,
    receipt=ReceiptType.READ,       # or DELIVERED
)

mark_read accepts several IDs at once for batch acknowledgement.

items.title: Typing Indicators
items.text:
Show a composing indicator while preparing an answer:

from neonize.utils.enum import ChatPresence, ChatPresenceMedia

client.send_chat_presence(chat, ChatPresence.COMPOSING, ChatPresenceMedia.TEXT)
# ... do work ...
client.send_chat_presence(chat, ChatPresence.PAUSED, ChatPresenceMedia.TEXT)

Raises SendPresenceError if the presence update fails.

items.title: Undecryptable Messages
items.text: If a message cannot be decrypted (e.g. sent with a protocol feature this build predates), you receive UndecryptableMessageEv instead of MessageEv. Register both when completeness matters.

items.title: Receipts for Outgoing Messages
items.text: After sending, acknowledgements arrive as ReceiptEv — delivered, read, or played — keyed by the original message ID returned in SendResponse.ID.

items.title: Sending Messages
items.text: All send methods accept a JID destination and return a SendResponse containing the message ID and send timestamp.

items.title: Text
items.text:
Pass a phone number string directly — it is auto-wrapped into a JID:

client.send_message("628123456789", "Hello from Neonize")

Or build a JID explicitly when you need a non-default server (e.g. groups):

from neonize.utils import build_jid

group = build_jid("120363001234567890", "g.us")
client.send_message(group, "Hello group")

send_message also accepts a raw protobuf Message, which every build_*_message method produces — this is how you compose advanced payloads.

items.title: Link previews
items.text:
client.send_message(
    chat, "Check out https://github.com/krypton-byte/neonize", link_preview=True
)

items.title: Mentions
items.text:
Pass a string containing @<number> mentions and supply the same numbers in ghost_mentions; set mentions_are_lids=True when the chat uses LID identifiers (common inside groups).

client.send_message(
    group_chat,
    "Ping @628123456789, please review.",
    ghost_mentions="628123456789",
)

items.title: Replies
items.text:
reply_message quotes an existing message. Pass the received MessageEv payload:

@client.event(MessageEv)
def on_message(client: NewClient, ev: MessageEv) -> None:
    if ev.Message.conversation == "hi":
        client.reply_message("Hello!", ev.Message)

Options include to= (override destination), reply_privately=True (answer in DM instead of the group), and link_preview.

items.title: Media
items.text:
client.send_image(chat, "photo.jpg", caption="Sunset")
client.send_video(chat, "clip.mp4", caption="Look")
client.send_audio(chat, "voice.ogg", ptt=True)          # push-to-talk
client.send_document(chat, "report.pdf", filename="Q3-report.pdf")
client.send_sticker(chat, "meme.png", name="Bot", packname="MyPack")

Every media method accepts local paths, bytes, or URLs — see Media Handling.

Albums send several images/videos as one gallery message:

client.send_album(chat, ["a.jpg", "b.jpg", "c.jpg"], caption="Holiday")

items.title: Contacts and Location
items.text: client.send_contact(chat, contact_name="Support", contact_number="628123456789")

items.title: Editing and Revoking
items.text:
resp = client.send_message(chat, "Typo hre")
client.edit_message(chat, resp.ID, Message(conversation="Typo here"))

# Unsend for everyone:
client.revoke_message(chat, sender=bot_jid, message_id=resp.ID)

build_revoke returns the revoke as a Message instead of sending it directly — useful when composing it into other payloads.

items.title: Reactions
items.text:
from neonize.client import NewClient

msg = client.send_message(chat, "React to me")
client.send_message(chat, client.build_reaction(chat, bot_jid, msg.ID, reaction="👍"))

An empty reaction="" removes an existing reaction.

items.title: Pinning Messages
items.text:
client.pin_message(chat, sender_jid, message_id, seconds=604800)  # 7 days

seconds=0 unpins.

items.title: Interactive Messages
items.text: For buttons, list pickers and catalog messages use neonize.ext.interactive_message builders with send_interactive_message(to, interactive_message) — see Interactive Messages and Polls.

items.title: Delivery Semantics
items.text:
• Methods block until WhatsApp acknowledges the message (sync client).
  • A raised SendMessageError means the send failed; nothing was silently dropped.
  • Incoming acknowledgements arrive later as ReceiptEv.
